body: Add inaccessible gaps between `BlockAllocator` shards so Linux keeps their writable regions in separate VMAs. This reduces contention on the VMA reference counter during first-touch page faults, which can bottleneck allocation and skew NUMA placement.

review_comments.body: I think these paths should be covered regardless of runner CPU count; this isn't blocking. With `(hardware_concurrency() + 3) / 4` shards, every case here expects zero guards on runners with 4 or fewer CPUs. The rollback check in `block_allocator_fault_injection.cpp` returns early unless there are at least 2 guards, requiring 9 or more CPUs. Small runners can therefore pass both without exercising protection or rollback. I would let the test helper choose the shard count so these paths run everywhere.

title: "NUMA-aware `BlockAllocator`" follow-up
